---
title: "Interfacing with Microcontrollers"
---

In the first two units of this course, we wrote programs that performed
calculations and made decisions. But everything our programs did stayed inside
the computer.

What if we wanted to turn on a light automatically when it gets dark? Or switch
off the AC when no one is in the room? Or start a water pump when a tank runs
low, and stop it when the tank is full?

Jobs like these are usually done by a small computer called a microcontroller.
In this unit, we'll use an ESP32 microcontroller and program it in MicroPython,
a version of Python designed for microcontrollers.

We'll learn how to:

- build simple electronic circuits and connect them to a microcontroller
- write programs that read sensors and control lights, displays and other devices

[Ready to get started?](introduction/what-is-a-microcontroller.qmd)
